description: Computes how often two independent judges (e.g. an automated engine and a human override) rated the same object differently, and -- where a later outcome exists to settle it -- reports engineRight and humanRight as two SEPARATE counts, never combined into one blended accuracy number (a system can be right most of the time overall and still wrong every single time a human bothers to overrule it, and that second fact is the one worth acting on). Divergence needs BOTH a count floor (minDivergentCount) and a rate floor (minDivergentRate) before it's 'reportable' -- either alone lets noise through. Calibration (who was right) carries its own separate floor (minResolvedDivergent) and its own status, so a population can legitimately have reportable divergence and refused calibration at the same time: plenty of disagreements, not enough of them settled by a later outcome yet. Supply `group` on each pair (a custom config.groupBySource is off unless the server operator sets HONESTY_MCP_ENABLE_CODE_EXEC=1) to also get a sorted per-group breakdown alongside the overall report. Use this whenever a system has both an automated judgment and a human override/correction recorded for the same objects, to find out whether overruling the system is actually earning its keep. For grading one recommendation's own before/after outcome window instead of a whole population of engine-vs-human calls, use grade_decision.

config.description: Floors, thresholds, and optional custom grouping, every field optional with a library default (see advice-ledger-kit's DEFAULT_DIVERGENCE_CONFIG). Omit entirely to use the library's defaults.

exampleLimit.description: How many divergent pairs to carry through as examples. Default 10.

minComparablePairs.description: Minimum pairs where both judges spoke. Default 10.

minDivergentRate.description: Minimum disagreement share of comparable pairs, 0 to 1. Default 0.05. Both this AND minDivergentCount must clear before divergence is 'reportable' -- either floor alone lets pure noise through (a 100% rate on 3 of 3 occasions, or a real rate buried in a huge sample).

minResolvedDivergent.description: Minimum disagreements that also have a later outcome, before naming who was right. Default 3.

pairs.description: Every occasion both judges could have spoken on. Pairs missing one judgment are still counted, just not comparable.

engineJudgment.description: What the system said. Compared to humanJudgment by exact equality -- use one canonical spelling per judgment. An empty string counts as 'didn't speak' for comparability purposes, same as omitting it.

group.description: Optional bucket, used by the default groupBy to produce the per-group breakdown. Ignored if config.groupBySource is supplied.

humanJudgment.description: What the human said. Same equality and 'didn't speak' treatment as engineJudgment.

id.description: Optional identifier, carried through into `examples` on a divergence report.

laterOutcome.description: What actually turned out to be the case, when that is known yet. Compared by exact equality against engineJudgment/humanJudgment to settle who was right on a divergent pair. Omit if not yet known.

name: compute_divergence
title: Measure where two judges disagree, and who was right
